title: Overdue-Cycle Allowance — Occupancy and Residency Certification Reclassification After Death
content:
The survivor allowance by which an Occupancy and Residency Certification profile's passed due date is re-dated on a reclassification after a certifying borrower's death includes an **overdue-cycle allowance**, which turns on two kinds of entry recorded under the open cycle (the certification year equal to the calendar year of the open cycle's due date):

| Recorded under the open cycle | Overdue-cycle allowance |
|---|---|
| an inspection finding of occupied by the borrower **and** a recorded certification | 21 days |
| exactly one of the two | 14 days |
| neither | zero days |

## Points of judgement

- Only an inspection finding of *occupied by the borrower* counts; a finding of vacant, occupied by others or unable to determine does not.
- Entries recorded under an earlier certification year do not count for the open cycle.
- *Hypothetical case.* The open cycle carries one recorded certification and no inspection finding: exactly one of the two is present, so the allowance is 14 days. Had an occupied-by-the-borrower finding also been recorded under that cycle, it would be 21 days.
